name: Synthetic Support Triage Guide
disclaimer: Project-authored synthetic guidance. It does not reproduce a real company's support policy, queues, SLA, legal duties, or customer-service handbook.

rules.title: Intent
rules.guidance: Record the user's main requested outcome separately from supporting intents.

rules.title: Category
rules.guidance: Choose one issue category without treating it as a confirmed real-world event.

rules.title: Urgency
rules.guidance: Use impact, time sensitivity, and possible risk; do not use sentiment intensity as urgency.

rules.title: Recommended queue
rules.guidance: Queue mappings are recommendations and never represent assignment or transfer.

rules.title: Escalation
rules.guidance: Possible safety, fraud, severe financial, or broad service impact normally warrants human escalation review.

rules.title: Next action
rules.guidance: Actions are recommendations only and do not mean work was performed.

rules.title: Unclear
rules.guidance: Use unclear classifications when evidence is insufficient and retain an explanation.

rules.title: Refund
rules.guidance: Refund requests normally go to refunds and cancellations or billing operations.

rules.title: Technical
rules.guidance: Technical reports normally go to technical support and may require logs.

rules.title: Account access
rules.guidance: Account access and security remain separate from ordinary profile changes.

rules.title: Safety
rules.guidance: Reported safety or abuse concerns require careful wording and appropriate human review.

rules.title: Fraud
rules.guidance: Reported fraud or security concerns are suspected concerns, not confirmed findings.

rules.title: Multiple intents
rules.guidance: Keep one primary intent and at most two supporting secondary intents.

rules.title: Mock suggestion
rules.guidance: Fixture suggestions are deterministic synthetic examples, not expert advice or model ground truth.
